title: A framework for holistic development of sustainability in higher education institutions
abstractText: Purpose Nations are implementing systematic approaches to achieve the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. Higher education institutions (HEIs) can serve as powerful catalysts in supporting these efforts and driving progress towards the agenda. However, existing Sustainable Assessment Tools (SATs) were unable to meet the needs of developing nations’ HEIs. This study aims to analyse five major SATs and propose a holistic Environmental Social and Governance (ESG)-aligned framework for HEIs, with India as a validation case study. Design/methodology/approach A mixed method approach was used, and data were collected from sources like research articles, ranking and accreditation agencies. Five SATs (QS, UI GM, THE, USAT and STARS) were classified and analysed. The qualitative method involved mapping SAT towards 169 indicators of Sustainable Development Goals (SDG). The quantitative method involved charting the proportion of the five SATs indicators and metrics towards ESG. Findings The analysis showed major contribution was towards environmental segment and less towards social and governance. Social SDGs, particularly SDG 8 (Decent work) and SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities) received near zero coverage. The proposed framework includes segments such as social, economic and governance which also aligns with SDGs. Originality/value To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this study is among the first to analyse five SATs through both SDG and ESG charting providing an analysis for existing gaps. The expected impact was highest in the environmental segment by curbing emissions to 5.7 from 7.1 kg CO2eq. per capita per day. Incorporating the proposed framework with a ranking body, like NIRF in India will promote sustainability in HEIs and eventually contribute towards the 2030 Agenda for sustainable development of the nation.

title: Iso-Seq enables discovery of novel isoform variants in human retina at single-cell resolution
abstractText: Recent single cell transcriptomic profiling of the human retina provided important insights into the genetic signals in heterogeneous retinal cell populations that enable vision. However, conventional single cell RNAseq with 3’ short-read sequencing is not suitable to identify isoform variants. Here we utilized Iso-Seq with full-length sequencing to profile the human retina at single cell resolution for isoform discovery. We generated a retina transcriptome dataset consisting of 25,302 nuclei from three donor retina, and detected 49,710 known transcripts and 241,949 novel transcripts across major retinal cell types. We surveyed the use of alternative promoters to drive transcript variant expression, and showed that 1-8% of genes utilized multiple promoters across major retinal cell types. Also, our results enabled gene expression profiling of novel transcript variants for inherited retinal disease (IRD) genes, and identified differential usage of exon splicing in major retinal cell types. Altogether, we generated a human retina transcriptome dataset at single cell resolution with full-length sequencing. Our study highlighted the potential of Iso-Seq to map the isoform diversity in the human retina, providing an expanded view of the complex transcriptomic landscape in the retina.

title: Exploring the barriers and pathways to sustainable adoption of virtual reality in architecture: a pilot study comparing industry and academic perspectives
abstractText: Purpose A central concern in the sustainable adoption of digital technologies is that, despite demonstrated technical benefits, their integration across the architecture, engineering and construction (AEC) sector remains uneven. Virtual reality (VR) exemplifies this challenge: although it has the potential to transform architectural communication, collaboration and design education, uptake is fragmented by competing institutional priorities and by users’ cognitive and affective experiences. This study aims to investigate how VR is perceived and applied in academia and practice. Design/methodology/approach The authors conducted focus group interviews analysed using causal layered analysis (CLA). During these sessions, academics and industry experts used VR headsets, and their experiences and reflections were transcribed and systematically coded for analysis. Findings Beyond surface observations, CLA reveals how psychological factors (e.g. presence, immersion, agency) interact with technical and organisational barriers. Six themes emerged across both groups: collaboration, immersion, immersivity, embodiment, accessibility and cultural resistance, highlighting areas of alignment and divergence. The findings demonstrate that VR adoption is not simply a technical process but a cultural and organisational negotiation, and they propose pathways for effectively embedding immersive technologies into architectural practice and education. Originality/value This paper offers an original, multi-layered account of VR adoption in architecture by applying CLA to bridge academic and industry perspectives. Rather than treating adoption as a purely technical issue, it reveals how cognitive, cultural and organisational dynamics shape uptake. The study introduces a novel distinction between immersion and immersivity, clarifying how user experience and system design operate across different layers. By identifying shared and divergent themes, it provides actionable pathways for aligning workflows, pedagogy and institutional cultures. The paper’s value lies in reframing VR adoption as a systemic negotiation, advancing more sustainable and context-sensitive integration strategies.

title: Cortical astrocytes flexibly encode reward contingencies and shape motivated response adaptation
abstractText: Learned associations between environmental cues and reward drive motivated behavior, yet how specific cell types support this process remains unclear. Using longitudinal two-photon calcium imaging, we tracked dorsal medial prefrontal cortical astrocytes throughout the acquisition, expression, and reversal of Pavlovian sucrose conditioning. As learning progressed, astrocytes exhibited time-locked, spatially coordinated calcium signals that differentiated correct behavioral action from mistakes, evolving from broad outcome encoding to selective representation of responses associated with the reward-conditioned stimulus. Omission testing revealed that prefrontal astrocytes preferentially respond to the cue-reward association, rather than the conditioned stimulus or reward alone. When reward contingencies were reversed, astrocytic activity rapidly adapted to track the new cue-reward association and encode updated and outdated motivated behavioral actions. Finally, astrocytic ablation attenuated motivated behavior during initial associative learning and prevented persistence of conditioned reward seeking when reward contingencies were updated or unpredictable. These findings reveal prefrontal astrocytes are functionally plastic elements that regulate reward-seeking behavior across associative learning. Teaser: Prefrontal astrocytes flexibly encode the cue-reward associations that drive conditioned reward-seeking behavior.

title: Cognitive decline in aging parasitoid wasps
abstractText: Aging induces observable cognitive decline in human and some other animals. For species that rely on learning and memory for reproduction, impaired cognitive functions may incur severe fitness costs. Here we report age-related cognitive decline in a solitary parasitoid wasp, Venturia canescens , in which reproductive females use olfactory memories for host seeking and selection. We trained female wasps to associate an odour with an oviposition reward, and compared their learning and memory performances at different ages, during the first half of the typical lifespan for this species. Wasps aged between 6 and 14 days showed consistently poorer learning and memory than their younger conspecifics, and this tendency increased with age. Such precocious cognitive decline in reproductive parasitoid wasps may have fitness consequences, through altered abilities to identify high quality hosts for offspring development.

title: Status of round goby invasion fronts in New York and Quebec: Implications for Lake Champlain
abstractText: The invasive round goby Neogobius melanostomus (Pallas, 1814) has advanced eastward through the state of New York and provinces of Ontario and Quebec over the past two decades and is approaching Lake Champlain, one of the largest lakes in North America. This manuscript describes international efforts to monitor round goby populations during 2021–2025 on (a) the southern approach to Lake Champlain via the Hudson River and Champlain Canal, and (b) the northern approach to Lake Champlain via the Saint Lawrence and Richelieu rivers. Monitoring utilized environmental DNA (eDNA), backpack electrofishing, beach seining, benthic trawling, and viral hemorrhagic septicemia virus (VHSV) testing. In the Champlain Canal, round gobies were captured as far north as the downstream side of the C1 dam (97 kilometers [km] from Lake Champlain) while eDNA detections occurred as far north as the upstream side of the C2 dam (90 km from Lake Champlain). In the Richelieu River, round gobies were captured as far south as Saint-Marc-sur-Richelieu (82 km from Lake Champlain) while the southernmost eDNA detections occurred near the Canadian side of the international border (4 km from Lake Champlain). Water temperature influenced round goby habitat use in the Champlain Canal, with catch rates in near-shore areas declining at < 10 °C. All VHSV test results were non-detections at the mouth of the Richelieu River, while one positive and two inconclusive results occurred along the Champlain Canal. Together, these data have informed multiple mitigation measures and have implications for management of aquatic invasive species across North America.

title: Screening for Prostate Cancer: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
abstractText: Background Previous recommendations on screening for prostate cancer relied on ongoing trials of screening with prostate-specific antigen (PSA), which may have lacked sufficient follow-up duration to fully examine effects on mortality and overdiagnosis. Findings which consider absolute effects by age and screening intensity, along with newer guidance for assessing evidence certainty, may lead to different interpretations. Adding magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to PSA-based screening has been raised as a way to reduce false positives (FPs) and overdiagnosis. Methods We systematically searched MEDLINE, Embase, and Central from 2014 to January 28, 2026, for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and prospective observational studies of: (i) screening versus no screening and (ii) sequential screening with MRI for those with a positive PSA test versus PSA alone among men not known to be at high risk for prostate cancer. Studies on screening with PSA or digital rectal examination (DRE) published pre-2014 were identified from existing systematic reviews and reference lists. Studies on FPs and complications from biopsies after PSA screening did not require a control group. Paired reviewers screened titles/abstracts (assisted with artificial intelligence) and full texts, assessed risk of bias, and extracted data, by age when available. We pooled data when suitable using random-effects models, investigated heterogeneity, and assessed the certainty of evidence using GRADE with conclusions of effects based on decision thresholds based on absolute effect sizes. Results Across both questions, we included 15 RCTs (N=856,000; 8 sites of ERSPC considered separate trials) and 8 observational studies (N=56,122). At 20 years, among 1000 men who underwent repeated PSA-based screening every 2-4 years starting from age 55-69 (mean 62), there is likely a reduction in prostate-cancer mortality (≥2 fewer) and metastatic cancer incidence (≥6 fewer), at the expense of prostate-cancer overdiagnosis (≥24 cases) and FPs (≥150 cases) (all moderate certainty). If screening starts at age 50-54 or age 55, the benefits are probably smaller (e.g., 1 vs. 2 fewer prostate-cancer related deaths) with similar harms. Adding DRE or screening with PSA annually does not add benefit. One round of PSA screening or starting screening later at age 70-74 may not offer any important benefit or harm (low to moderate certainty), and any benefit from screening primarily with DRE was not shown. Compared with PSA alone, sequential screening with PSA followed by MRI reduces FPs (≥33 fewer) and overdiagnosis (via ≥10 fewer diagnoses of clinically insignificant [e.g., Gleason 6] cancers without impacting detection of clinically significant cancers) (moderate to high certainty), though findings were limited to one round of screening without long-term follow-up or measurement of mortality. Interpretation This review provides clinicians and other interest holders with anticipated absolute effects by age, and assessments of certainty across critical and important outcomes and with approximately two decades of follow-up. Findings apply to a general population and may differ for specific groups. Results for most critical outcomes, both benefits and harms, exceeded thresholds for clinically important effect sizes, thereby demonstrating the complexity of guideline developers’ and patients’ decision-making regarding screening trade-offs. Findings about adding MRI for those with a positive PSA test were limited and would require additional consideration of costs, infrastructure, expertise, and equity. title: Multimodal signal restoration with signed twofold graph learning
abstractText: The authors propose a method for jointly learning signed twofold graphs and performing signal restoration on multimodal graph signals. Multimodal signals on sensor networks are commonly modeled under the twofold graph assumption (TGA), which represents spatial structure and inter-modality relations as two separate graphs. Existing TGA-based signal restoration methods, however, either assume the graphs are known or restrict edge weights to be non-negative, preventing them from capturing negative inter-modal correlations. The authors address both limitations as follows. To learn twofold graphs from noisy and incomplete data, the authors formulate joint signal restoration and twofold graph learning as MAP estimation under a matrix normal prior, where the spatial and modality graph Laplacians appear directly as precision matrices. The resulting non-convex objective is solved by alternating minimization: the signal is updated via conjugate gradient applied to the arising Sylvester-type linear system; the graphs are updated via primal-dual hybrid gradient (PDHG). To capture negative inter-modal correlations, we estimate the signed structure of the modality graph from the dominant eigenspace of a complementary kernel matrix, which is then used in PDHG to update edge magnitudes. These iterative solvers are then unrolled into a feedforward network, with regularization weights and step sizes as layer-wise trainable parameters. Experiments on synthetic multimodal graph signals and two real-world data sets (Japan meteorological and Beijing air-quality data) confirm that the proposed method outperforms existing baselines across a range of noise levels and missing-data patterns; the learned graphs are also directly validated against the ground-truth graphs on the synthetic data sets.

title: Spatially resolved optical and mid-infrared spectroscopy of SDSS1335+0728: Implications for the origin of the Ansky event
abstractText: The galaxy SDSS1335+0728 brightened abruptly in December 2019 (i.e. the event) and it has since been confirmed as the host of extreme X-ray quasi-periodic eruptions (QPEs) whose origins are currently the subject of debate. We constrained the origin of its transient activity using spatially resolved VLT/MUSE and JWST MIRI/MRS spectroscopy to characterise the host galaxy and its nuclear accretion history. The stellar kinematics reveal two counter-rotating stellar components and kinematically cold gas (σ_ Ansky ̊m gas łesssim 60 km s -1 $) consistent with a past minor merger. The host is dominated by old stars, with ongoing star formation confined to a ring at intermediate radii. Ionisation diagnostics reveal a three-zone structure: a central accretion-powered region, where high-ionisation coronal lines ( Ne VI , Ne V , O IV ) are predominantly concentrated, along with a star-forming ring and a LINER-like outer region. A Balmer-line light-echo analysis yields a minimum ionising luminosity of łog L_ ̊m ion,min ≈ 40.5 erg s^-1 at projected distances beyond the reach of radiation from the event, suggesting nuclear activity prior to 2019. Strong silicate emission at 9.7 and 18,μm indicates directly illuminated dust viewed through a low effective mid-infrared (MIR) optical depth; its 9.7,μm strength lies at the upper end of the active galactic nucleus (AGN) distribution, bringing it closer to that of MIR-selected tidal disruption events (TDEs). The data are consistent with pre-2019 accretion from either a low-luminosity AGN (LLAGN) or a long-lived TDE remnant disc. In both cases, Ansky Ansky is posited as a slow, faint transient in a $∼!10^6,M_⊙ black hole with ongoing accretion prior to December 2019, offering an alternative to the so-called faded AGN interpretation that has been proposed for some QPE hosts.

title: When Parasorex met Schizogalerix? The early Late Miocene insectivorans and a bat from Sütlüce (Çanakkale, Türkiye)
abstractText: The locality of Sütlüce yielded three eulipotyphlans, the gymnures Parasorex voesendorfensis and Schizogalerix sinapensis , as well as the shrew Crusafontina endemica , and an unidentified vespertilionid bat. On the basis of the presence of S. sinapensis and the stage of evolution of C. endemica , an age around the early/late Vallesian boundary can be postulated. The combination in a single locality of a species of Parasorex and Schizogalerix , two morphologically similar forms, is unique. This appears to be part of a biogeographical pattern in which the European Parasorex had a short excursion to the east in the Vallesian at the same time that the Anatolian Schizogalerix started expanding its distribution to the west. This suggests that Sütlüce promises to be a key locality in reconstructing the distributional changes at a time when the Greco-Iranian bioprovince was growing in influence.

title: AGNFormer. I: Reconstruction of active galactic nucleus spectra using a probabilistic transformer model
abstractText: When analysing spectroscopic data to extract physical properties, emphasis is often placed on small portions of a spectrum (e.g. ionisation diagnostic diagrams, broad Hβ or Mg ii emission lines, etc.), potentially discarding a wealth of useful information. We explore how an uncertainty-aware transformer-based architecture can leverage information embedded across the entire observed optical spectra of active galactic nuclei (AGNs), focussing on the algorithm's ability to predict unseen or masked parts of luminous AGN spectra, providing a direct probe of the learnable correlations between AGN continua and broad lines. We introduce AGNFormer -1 $; missing halves), inputting rest-frame spectral fluxes and uncertainties across the entire redshift range of the SDSS DR16 Quasar Catalogue. We evaluate the performance of the model on both full (no S/N limit) and high-quality (S/N $> 10) spectral samples using the negative-log likelihood and via comparisons with existing ̧iv and łyman reconstruction algorithms. The model successfully reconstructs unseen AGN broad lines up to an error floor of ≈2-6% of the flux at S/N ≈ 40, while the predictive power for larger unseen halves diminishes with distance from the cut-off wavelength of the input spectrum. Predictions faithfully reproduce the broad AGN spectral diversity across the entire optical and UV quasi-stellar object (QSO) main sequence parameter spaces, including both Gaussian and Lorentzian profile regimes, complexes, and narrow emission lines. The performance is found to be similar or better compared to previous spectral reconstruction algorithms. The high precision of the broad-line region reconstruction demonstrates that the method successfully aggregates information across the spectrum and highlights how the AGN continuum as well as weaker lines and complexes have the potential to assist astronomers in the extraction of the entire wealth of information embedded in AGN spectra. title: Circumgalactic medium depletion drives satellite quenching in IllustrisTNG
abstractText: Satellite galaxies dominate the quenched population at low and intermediate stellar masses (M_⋆ $,łesssim,$$ 10.5 ,̊m M_⊙$), yet determining the processes that shut down their star formation, their relative importance, and on what timescales they occur remain a central problem in galaxy evolution. We used MaNGA-like mock galaxies from IllustrisTNG to dissect different satellite quenching pathways, paying special attention to the role of the circumgalactic medium (CGM) during the quenching phase. With a merger tree-based algorithm, we reconstructed the baryonic, dark matter, structural, and chemical histories of ∼7,300 spatially resolved galaxies (2,800 satellites) along their SubLink trees, using time since infall as the physical axis along which quenching unfolds. We observed that satellites retain regular rotation-supported stellar kinematics throughout quenching, with disturbed velocity fields confined to systems with M_⋆ $,łesssim,$$ 10^ 10.5 ,̊m M_⊙$. For the first time, we present the coupled time evolution of the depletion of both the hot and cool gas reservoirs after infall. Based on our results, satellites lose ∼90% of their hot CGM within ∼3.7^ +0.6 _ -0.6 ,Gyr. This loss increases with residence time and is independent of stellar mass. The hot gas mass correlates strongly with the star formation rate, identifying the CGM as a long-term fuel reservoir. In contrast, quenched centrals retain massive hot halos, likely sustained by active galactic nuclei feedback. The present-day quenched satellites have been satellites for more time than star-forming ones (5.9 +0.3 _ -0.3 $ versus 3.7^ +0.2 _ -0.2 ,Gyr), forming stars for at least $∼3.7,Gyr after infall before declining sharply, which is consistent with a delayed-then-rapid quenching scenario. Losing little stellar mass yet with their gas depleted and their dark matter and metal-poor stellar outskirts tidally stripped, satellites emerge more compact and metal rich than centrals at a fixed mass. Our results suggest the gradual erosion of the hot CGM as the key link connecting infall to the slow shutdown of star formation.

title: Recent Advances in Microstrip Antenna Design, Advanced Substrate Materials, and Intelligent Optimization Techniques: A Comprehensive Review
abstractText: Microstrip antennas are very important in modern wireless communication systems due to their small size, low cost of manufacturing and easy integration with electronic devices. With the continuous development of wireless technologies, the demand for antennas with better bandwidth, gain, radiation efficiency, miniaturization and intelligent design capability is growing. This paper provides a detailed narrative review on the recent developments in microstrip antenna technology in three complementary research areas: antenna design techniques, advanced substrate materials, and intelligent design and optimization methods. The recent studies were systematically gathered and analyzed, and compared critically based on the design methodologies, material characteristics, antenna performance, optimization approaches, practical applications, and reported limitations. As revealed by the review, innovative structural designs, engineered substrate materials and artificial intelligence based optimization techniques have been able to enhance the performance of the antennas while minimizing the complexity of the designs and the development time. Important research challenges are also identified, such as the need for multi-objective optimization, standardized evaluation methods, wider experimental validation, and better incorporation of advanced materials with intelligent optimization techniques. In general, the review shows that the integration of structural innovation, substrate engineering and intelligent computational methods is an effective way for the development of next generation microstrip antennas. The results provide a single reference for researchers and engineers to design compact, efficient, and intelligent antennas for future applications such as 5G and 6G, the Internet of Things, satellite communications, wearable electronics, and millimeter-wave wireless systems.

title: How Classification Models Degrade as Data Diminish: A Multi-Criteria Analysis of Tabular Classifiers Under Controlled Data Scarcity
abstractText: Machine learning research is frequently conducted under an implicit assumption of data abundance, yet applied software development often proceeds under severe data constraints. This study evaluated how five widely used classification algorithms—logistic regression, support vector machines, Gaussian naive Bayes, decision trees, and random forests—degrade when training data are systematically reduced. Eight tabular datasets drawn from the UCI Machine Learning Repository, spanning small, medium, and large volume tiers, were analysed within a quantitative comparative experimental design. Training folds were reduced to 100%, 75%, 50%, and 25% of their original size through stratified fractional sampling inside a stratified five-fold cross-validation loop, while validation folds were retained at full volume. Ten criteria were recorded: accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, AUC-ROC, AUC-PR, mean absolute error and mean squared error of predicted probabilities, training time, and interpretability. One-way analyses of variance and Tukey honestly significant difference tests were applied at an alpha level of .05. Between-model differences were statistically significant in 31 of 32 dataset-by-volume configurations. Tree-based models exhibited the largest reductions in accuracy and the steepest increases in calibration error under scarcity, whereas logistic regression preserved threshold balance and probability calibration at negligible computational cost. Random forests attained the highest scores only when data were abundant. Pairwise comparisons aggregated across datasets were not significant, indicating that dataset context, rather than architectural complexity alone, governs absolute performance.

title: In Love with the Interface: otome Game Engagement and the Psychosocial Development of Young Adult Cisgender Filipinas
abstractText: This study examined the relationship between otome game engagement and the psychosocial development of young adult cisgender Filipinas. Guided by Parasocial Interaction Theory, Identity Development Theory, and Uses and Gratifications Theory, the study employed a quantitative correlational design to assess whether usage frequency, emotional investment (parasocial processing), and financial investment (in-game content purchase motivation) were associated with identity development, psychological well-being, real-life social interaction, and real-life romantic expectations. A total of 118 young adult cisgender Filipinas (aged 18 to 25) who were active otome game players were recruited through purposive and snowball sampling from online otome gaming communities and university networks. Data were collected using a structured online questionnaire incorporating validated and researcher-developed scales, and analyzed using Spearman's rho correlation and multiple linear regression. Results indicated that usage frequency, parasocial processing, and in-game content purchase motivation were significantly and positively associated with real-life social interaction and romantic expectations, and that parasocial processing and in-game purchase motivation significantly predicted identity development. However, none of the engagement variables significantly predicted psychological well-being. These findings suggest that otome game engagement, particularly emotional and financial investment, is meaningfully linked to identity exploration, social experience, and romantic perception among young adult Filipinas, while exerting limited measurable influence on general psychological well-being.

title: Composition-tuned Ni exsolution from Ruddlesden–Popper oxides for durable CO2 dry reforming of methane
abstractText: Nickel exsolution from complex oxides yields socketed metal nanoparticles, but the working structure of such catalysts under dry reforming of methane (DRM) and its evolution during prolonged operation remain poorly resolved. Here, a compositional series of n = 2 (La,Sr)₃(Mn,Ni)₂O₇ Ruddlesden–Popper oxides was reduced to generate partially embedded Ni nanoparticles on an n = 1-derived oxide matrix. Mean particle diameters are similar across the series (~35–39 nm), separating compositional effects from particle-size effects. At 850 °C and GHSV = 3.0 × 10⁴ mL gcat⁻¹ h⁻¹, all catalysts sustain DRM for 168 h, reaching up to 86% CH₄ and 88% CO₂ conversion, with activity not scaling with nominal Ni loading. In situ neutron powder diffraction on the L150N50 reference under CH₄/CO₂ shows the n = 1 matrix and metallic Ni remaining dominant over 12 h from 850 to 700 °C, the refined Ni fraction staying within ~5.6–6.3 wt.%, without phase reconstruction or crystalline SrCO₃ and graphitic carbon. Tests extended to ~550 h instead reveal temperature- and composition-dependent deactivation with slower support reconstruction, showing that post-reaction multiphase states reflect long-term ageing rather than the initial working structure. Carbon accumulation stays limited and spatially heterogeneous, CO₂-TPSR gives CO from pre-adsorbed CO₂ near 700 °C, and Ni preferentially associates with La-enriched domains while Sr-rich regions are Ni-poor. DRM activity and durability therefore arise from the coupled behaviour of socketed Ni and an evolving La/Sr oxide matrix, rather than from Ni loading alone.

title: Euclid. XI. A two-point correlation approach to diagnosing star-related systematics in the spectroscopic survey
abstractText: The Euclid spectroscopic survey will measure galaxy clustering with unprecedented precision, which demands stringent control over observational and instrumental systematics. Among these, star-related effects may contaminate the spectroscopic images through photometric persistence and through imperfect masking of stellar images. We characterized the imprint of star-related effects in the spectroscopic exposures and quantified their impact on galaxy clustering analyses. If these effects produce characteristic angular features, they can be identified and characterized in the data, thereby enabling an assessment of their impact on cosmological measurements. We used angular and spatial auto- and cross-correlation statistics to quantify these effects. For the galaxies we used mock spectroscopic catalogues extracted from EuclidLargeMocks. We focused on a 330 region of the Euclid Wide Survey (EWS). For the stars, we considered the real Gaia and star catalogues in the same area. To simulate photometric persistence, we implemented a simplified detector-level model calibrated on spectroscopic measurements and modulated the strength of the effect to introduce varying fractions of `interlopers' into the mock galaxy catalogues. For the stellar mask, we modelled potential inconsistencies between the mask used to remove regions around stars in the data and the mask applied to the random catalogue used to quantify the survey selection function. We measured the star--star, galaxy--galaxy, and star--galaxy angular correlation functions using the Landy--Szalay estimator and quantified deviations from the expected null star–galaxy correlation with a dedicated metric. Finally, we evaluated the impact of these systematics on large scales using the 3D two-point correlation function (2PCF). Our results show that photometric persistence produces a characteristic feature in the star--galaxy angular cross-correlation at scales of order 100 consistent with the scale set by the Euclid dithering pattern and grism dispersion geometry. It also induces a spurious, positive cross-correlation signal that remains approximately constant in amplitude up to 1^̧irc. We find that star–galaxy cross-correlation analysis is a sensitive tool for detecting residual persistence and is capable of revealing spurious contamination levels as low as 10% in a Data Release 1-like spectroscopic catalogue. In contrast, mismatches in stellar masking produce strong small-scale angular signatures but do not significantly impact the large-scale 2PCF under realistic EWS conditions.

title: Assistance in Arabic Language Learning through the Singing Method for Students of Madrasah Diniyah Al-Ittihad, Subang
abstractText: This study aims to improve students’ interest in learning Arabic and their ability to understand and apply Arabic learning materials through singing. The activity was conducted from August 10 to 14, 2026, at Madrasah Diniyah Al-Ittihad, Cidahu Village, involving fourth-grade students. The implementation employed a participatory mentoring approach consisting of identification, planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation stages. Initial data were obtained through observation and interviews, while the learning activities integrated singing, question-and-answer sessions, educational games, repetition, individual mentoring, and simple communicative practices. The results indicate positive responses and increased student engagement, reflected in their enthusiasm, active interaction, and ability to recall and apply the learning materials in simple communication. The novelty of this study lies in integrating singing with participatory mentoring and communicative practice as an enjoyable and applicable strategy for Arabic language learning. Thus, this approach can serve as an interactive and contextual alternative for Arabic language instruction in madrasah diniyah.

title: Public assistance program participation and overweight and obesity among low-income California adults: a repeated cross-sectional analysis of the California Health Interview Survey, 2019–2024
abstractText: Background Participation in public assistance programs may be associated with weight outcomes among low-income adults, but associations may differ by program type and sex. We examined associations of participation in the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), Supplemental Security Income (SSI), and California Work Opportunity and Responsibility to Kids (CalWORKs) with overweight and obesity among low-income California adults and evaluated differences by sex. Methods We analyzed 2019–2024 California Health Interview Survey (CHIS) data among adults with household income at or below 130% of the federal poverty level ( n = 16,918). Survey-weighted logistic regression estimated adjusted odds ratios (AORs) for overweight (BMI 25.0–29.9 kg/m²) and obesity (BMI ≥ 30.0 kg/m²), each compared with BMI < 25.0 kg/m², adjusted for sociodemographic characteristics, smoking, insurance, and food insecurity, with sex-stratified models and formal interaction tests. Results SNAP participation was associated with higher odds of obesity (AOR = 1.23; 95% CI = 1.07–1.42) but not overweight; the association was concentrated among females (AOR = 1.37; 95% CI = 1.15–1.64; P for interaction = 0.04). CalWORKs participation was associated with higher odds of overweight (AOR = 1.29; 95% CI = 1.05–1.59) but not obesity, and this association did not differ significantly by sex. SSI was not significantly associated with either outcome. Conclusions Associations varied by program type and outcome. The stronger SNAP–obesity association among women likely identifies a high-burden subgroup rather than a sex-specific program effect, and these cross-sectional associations likely reflect selection into programs rather than program effects. Further research is needed to elucidate underlying mechanisms and to inform policies that support healthy weight.

title: Spectral arithmetic over orthomodular lattices
abstractText: Spectral families provide a representation of observables in quantum logic. This paper develops an addition operation for bounded spectral quantities over orthomodular lattices to examine the relation between familiar arithmetic behavior and lattice structure. The operation extends the established addition of bounded observables. Under this operation, bounded spectral quantities form an abelian group precisely when the lattice is Boolean. Conjugating the operation by spectral negation yields a dual sum, and equality of the primal and dual sums characterizes modularity. A modular non-Boolean example separates these two regimes concretely.

title: P2D - A Two-Dimensional Multi-Spacecraft Solar Wind Persistence Model
abstractText: The background solar wind is a key component in space weather forecasting, as it contains geoeffective high-speed streams and provides the medium through which coronal mass ejections propagate and evolve in interplanetary space. Due to the solar rotation and the slow evolution of large-scale solar wind structures, solar wind properties exhibit an autocorrelation with a period of roughly 27 days, particularly at solar minimum. We made use of this property to develop a solar wind persistence model with input from multiple spacecraft (Solar Orbiter, Parker Solar Probe, STEREO-A, STEREO-B and the OMNI database). The model ballistically propagates in-situ data from the position of their measurement radially away from the Sun, as well as longitudinally with the solar rotation rate, producing 2D maps of solar wind parameters. These can be extracted at any point in the heliosphere for a solar wind reconstruction. From Earth’s perspective, the reconstruction performs with an MAE of 65.41 km~s$^{-1}$ and 3.51 $cm^{-3}$ for speed and density, respectively. During high-speed streams, the peak hit rate is 50\% and 48\% for speed and density. It performs best during times when there are spacecraft located between Earth and Lagrange point L5. During these times, the mean absolute error of the predicted solar wind velocity decreases by roughly 35\% in comparison to the benchmark 27-day persistence model. Therefore, future L5 missions like Vigil are expected to provide a robust basis for reliable persistence forecasts.

title: The ALPINE-CRISTAL-JWST Survey: Investigating the role of interstellar dust, gas, and stars in high-z galaxies at kiloparsec scales
abstractText: A comprehensive understanding of galaxy evolution requires a detailed analysis of gas and dust, including their distribution and evolution within galaxies. In this work, we analyse spatially resolved (∼,1-2,kpc) rest-frame C ii and dust continuum ALMA observations together with JWST/NIRSpec IFU data of a sample of six massive galaxies at z,∼,4-5. We focus on deriving and comparing the spatial distributions of atomic and molecular gas masses, dust and stellar masses, star formation rates (SFR), and metallicity. The oxygen abundance maps have median values in the range of 12+log(O/H),sim8.1-8.3 with variations of the order of 1,dex within the same galaxy. In four galaxies of our sample, the oxygen abundance shows a minimum at the peak of the Hα emission and an enhancement in the outer parts. The calibration used in this study to estimate the atomic gas mass in our galaxies seems to overestimate the atomic gas mass surface densities by up to one to two orders of magnitude. However, a calibration based on a spatially resolved C ii conversion factor gives a more robust estimation of the total gas mass. The dust-to-gas surface mass density ratio varies between łog Σ_ ̊m dust /Σ_ ̊m gas =-2.2 ^ +0.24 _ -0.19 and łogΣ_ ̊m dust /Σ_ ̊m gas =-2.69^ +0.21 _ -0.16 , while the dust-to-stellar surface mass density ratio ranges from łogΣ_ ̊m dust /Σ_ ̊m star =-2.01^ +0.13 _ -0.12 to łogΣ_ ̊m dust /Σ_ ̊m star =-2.91^ +0.13 _ -0.13 . A detailed analysis of the dust-to-stellar surface mass density ratio and the gas mass fraction versus metallicity revealed that galaxies exhibiting signatures of strong outflows have a lower dust-to-stellar surface mass density ratio and lower gas mass fractions than the galaxies with no outflow signatures. While the latter is consistent with these galaxies ejecting part of their gas reservoir to the circumgalactic medium, the low dust-to-stellar surface mass density ratios also suggest that part of the dust content is expelled outside the galaxy, which reinforces previous theoretical suggestions of dust removal by stellar feedback or radiation pressure to explain the high UV luminosities in galaxies at very high redshifts. Some galaxies of our sample have almost an order of magnitude higher ratios of dust-to-gas and dust-to-stellar surface mass density than galaxies in the local Universe, suggesting that a large dust reservoir has been built up already at timescales of sim1,Gyr in these galaxies.

title: Surveying for close binaries among lithium-rich giants
abstractText: The existence of low-mass giants with high lithium (Li) abundances poses a challenge to our understanding of post-main sequence stellar structure and evolution. Li-rich giants are preferentially found in the red clump (RC) rather than on the first-ascent red giant branch (RGB). One of the scenarios proposed to explain this Li enrichment involves tidal interaction with a close binary companion, which, if dominant, predicts an enhanced binary fraction among Li-rich giants relative to Li-normal ones. We aim to test the binary interaction scenario for the origin of Li-rich giants by using multi-epoch radial velocities (RVs) in order to measure the close binary fraction of a statistically robust sample of Li-rich giants. The surveyed sample contains both RC and RGB targets, which allows us to examine potential differences in the binary fraction as a function of evolutionary stage. We monitored 70 giants (40 RC and 30 RGB) using the ESPRESSO spectrograph, 57 (32 RC and 25 RGB) of which already had four or more visits over a ∼7-month baseline. The analysis presented here is based on these latter targets. We first used a criterion based on surface gravity and the maximum observed RV difference within our data in order to discard RV variations attributable to intrinsic stellar jitter. For the targets with RV variation larger than this threshold, we performed Monte Carlo simulations over a grid of companion mass and orbital period, to estimate the probability that the observed RV variation is due to a stellar (P_SB) or substellar (P_SS) companion. After removing targets consistent with stellar jitter, 11 (34 ± 8%) RC and eight (32 ± 9%) RGB stars remained as binary candidates or stars with a companion. Of these, three targets (16 ± 8% of the filtered sample) are confirmed stellar binaries. The distributions of P_SB and P_SS are statistically indistinguishable between the RC and RGB samples. We find no evidence in our current data for a binary fraction for Li-rich giants (in either evolutionary stage) larger than that expected for a regular Li-normal population, which suggests that binary interaction is unlikely to be the dominant mechanism driving Li enrichment in this sample. Extending the RV baseline to probe longer orbital periods will be important to continue exploring the plausibility of this scenario.

title: Assessment of Vigilance Recovery in Rats after Anesthesia Using a Touchscreen-based Continuous Performance Task
abstractText: BACKGROUND: Cognitive recovery after general anesthesia is clinically important but incompletely understood. Rodent studies in anesthesia research have primarily examined memory and learning, while vigilance and other neurocognitive domains remain underexplored. To address this gap, the authors employed the rodent continuous performance task (rCPT), a touchscreen-based translational paradigm, to characterize anesthetic-specific recovery trajectories of vigilance after anesthetic emergence. METHODS: Sixteen adult Sprague-Dawley rats (eight male, eight female) were trained to proficiency on the rCPT. Once trained, loss of righting was induced by sevoflurane (3% for 20 min), propofol (10 mg/kg iv bolus), ketamine (50 mg/kg iv during 10 min), or dexmedetomidine (20 µg/kg iv bolus), delivered in a randomized order every other week. Animals were placed supine in the cognitive testing chamber and their performance was recorded for 4 h. Return of righting reflex (RORR) was used to indicate anesthetic emergence. Vigilance recovery was defined as 20 consecutive trials with an average hit rate greater than 0.6. RESULTS: The latency to recover vigilance was delayed after ketamine and dexmedetomidine compared to baseline (hazard ratio in ketamine, 5.34; 95% CI, 2.07 to 13.76; hazard ratio in dexmedetomidine, 5.33; 95% CI, 2.08 to 13.62; both P < .0001). Reward retrieval latency recovered 4 h after RORR after ketamine (percent change from baseline, -24.14%; 95% CI, -54.69 to 17.89%) but not recover at the same time point after dexmedetomidine (percent change from baseline, -47.85%; 95% CI, -71.94 to -20.23%). CONCLUSIONS: The rCPT identified delayed recovery of vigilance after ketamine and dexmedetomidine. Dexmedetomidine showed prolonged impairment across behavioral measures, including visual processing speed (hit latency) and reward retrieval, suggesting sustained effects on psychomotor function, motor coordination, and behavioral engagement that persisted for at least 4 h after RORR. These findings support the utility of the rCPT as a translational paradigm for characterizing agent-specific and domain-specific trajectories of cognitive recovery after anesthesia.

title: Comprehensive prognostic value of prealbumin and albumin in hepatocellular carcinoma resection: Insights from a Chinese multicenter cohort
abstractText: BACKGROUND Albumin and prealbumin are established prognostic factors for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but their combined impact on post-resection long-term outcomes requires further clarification. AIM To compare the impact of albumin, prealbumin, and their combination on long-term postoperative outcomes in HCC patients. METHODS The various impacts of albumin (low < 40 g/L, or normal ≥ 40 g/L) and prealbumin (low < 170 mg/L, or normal ≥ 170 mg/L) on overall survival (OS) and recurrence-free survival (RFS) for HCC patients following partial hepatectomy were comprehensively analyzed using a multi-institutional database. RESULTS During a median follow-up of 64.1 months, 892 recurrences and 675 deaths were recorded. Significant differences in OS and RFS were observed across the four groups (all P < 0.001). Compared with Group I (normal albumin and prealbumin), Group II (low albumin, normal prealbumin), Group III (normal albumin, low prealbumin), and Group IV (low albumin and low prealbumin) had shorter OS [Group II: hazard ratio (HR) = 1.37, 95%CI: 1.07-1.76; Group III: HR = 1.89, 95%CI: 1.49-2.39; Group IV: HR = 2.46, 95%CI: 2.02-2.99] and RFS (Group II: HR = 1.25, 95%CI: 1.02-1.54; Group III: HR = 1.65, 95%CI: 1.34-2.02; Group IV: HR = 1.95, 95%CI: 1.64-2.32). Multivariable analysis showed prealbumin was a dominant prognostic predictor for OS and RFS than albumin. When both markers were included, albumin lost independent prognostic value, while low prealbumin (regardless of albumin) remained an independent risk factor for worse OS and RFS. After adjusting for confounders, Group IV had the highest adjusted HR for reduced OS (1.65, 95%CI: 1.34-2.02, P < 0.001) and RFS (1.33, 95%CI: 1.10-1.60, P = 0.002). Time-dependent area under the curve analysis demonstrated that the combined stratification consistently outperformed albumin across all time points (all P < 0.001), with prealbumin showing modestly superior discrimination to albumin. CONCLUSION Prealbumin outperforms albumin as a prognostic biomarker for long-term survival after HCC resection. Combining prealbumin and albumin enables precise risk stratification, aiding surgical decision-making and patient counseling. This prealbumin-based risk stratification approach may help optimize perioperative management and identify high-risk patients.

title: Searching for nearby supermassive black hole binaries with GRAVITY
abstractText: We present a systematic interferometric search for close supermassive black hole (SMBH) binaries in 20 nearby type 1 active galactic nuclei (AGN) observed with <16.5% for <9.2%. title: Three S’s (sex, seniors, and sarcopenia) matter during chemotherapy for colorectal cancer
abstractText: Recent progress in treatments has dramatically improved the outcomes of colorectal cancer (CRC). Neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (CRT) has been the standard therapy for resectable advanced cancer of the lower rectum, and the combination of additional systemic chemotherapy before or after CRT is attracting attention for further improvement of local antitumor effects. Patients with unresectable CRC have a good chance of conversion to resection after the use of key cytotoxic drugs, such as 5-fluorouracil, oxaliplatin, and irinotecan, along with targeted antibodies. Furthermore, immune checkpoint inhibitors are available in these neoadjuvant settings. For adjuvant chemotherapy of localized CRC, the recommended treatment is 5-fluorouracil plus oxaliplatin. Meanwhile, accumulating evidence shows that sarcopenia is associated with adherence to and outcomes of these treatments. For instance, sarcopenia or skeletal muscle loss occurring before and during preoperative treatments predict poor prognosis in patients undergoing neoadjuvant CRT and those who received conversion therapy for unresectable CRC. Sarcopenia or skeletal muscle loss is also associated with dose-limiting toxicity and the outcomes of adjuvant chemotherapy. Importantly, unchangeable variables such as age and sex often determine sarcopenia and/or chemotherapy tolerability. This review describes the clinical significance of the three S’s (sex, seniors, and sarcopenia) in chemotherapy/CRT used in various settings for CRC.

title: The Pristine survey. XXIX. Data Release 2: Photometric metallicities for 15 millions stars down to G∼ 20.3
abstractText: Tailored narrowband photometric observations are an efficient way to measure the metallicity of Milky Way stars. The Pristine survey has been mapping the northern sky since 2015 using narrowband CaHK photometry obtained with the MegaCam imager on the Canada-France-Hawaii Telescope (CFHT). The Pristine Data Release 1 (DR1) provided a high-precision absolute calibration of the survey observed before October 2022 using Gaia DR3 XP synthetic photometry, yielding photometric metallicities over ∼6500 deg2$, but was limited in depth to the availability of Gaia spectro-photometry ($G łesssim 17.65). We present the Pristine Data Release 2 (DR2) that includes all Pristine observations until January 2025, corresponding to an additional 1500,deg2$ of coverage, and including all faint sources down to $G This release aims to exploit the full depth of the Pristine observations to uncover the faint metal-poor halo. We process all images observed from the start of the survey in March 2015 through to January 2025 following the methodology presented in DR1. The core of the calibration utilizes the subset of bright stars with Gaia synthetic CaHK_ neural network. We then derive photometric metallicities using the established Pristine (CaHK, G, G_ magnitudes to train the PhotCalib ̊m BP , G_ ̊m RP ) to FeH model. The resulting catalog covers approximately ∼ 8000 deg 2 and provides photometric metallicities for 15 million FGK stars, which show good agreement with recently published independent Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) metallicities. With its increased coverage and access to a significantly fainter regime compared to DR1, DR2 significantly increases the volume of the survey. We report more than 200,000 and 6500 very and extremely metal-poor star candidates, respectively.

title: HN1 L promotes colorectal cancer proliferation and migration by inhibiting the Hippo pathway
abstractText: BACKGROUND Postoperative recurrence and metastasis significantly hinder long-term survival in colorectal cancer (CRC), with varied responses to adjuvant chemotherapy observed among patients possessing similar clinical characteristics. HN1 L has been implicated in the progression of several malignancies; however, its biological function, regulatory mechanism, and clinical relevance in CRC remain inadequately defined. AIM To characterize the expression pattern and oncogenic function of HN1 L in CRC, investigate its association with Hippo signaling, and explore its association with postoperative risk stratification and adjuvant chemotherapy selection. METHODS HN1 L expression and clinical relevance were assessed using transcriptomic and clinical data from The Cancer Genome Atlas, single-cell RNA sequencing data from GSE132465, immunohistochemical (IHC) analyses of 84 paraffin-embedded CRC specimens, and an independent cohort comprising 10 paired frozen CRC and adjacent normal tissues for Western blot (WB). Stable HN1 L -overexpressing and knockdown CRC cell lines underwent quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction, WB, RNA sequencing, pathway enrichment analysis, as well as proliferation and migration assays. In vivo tumor-promoting effects of HN1 L were evaluated using xenograft models and IHC. Kaplan-Meier analysis, time-dependent receiver operating characteristic curves, Cox regression, and HN1 L expression-by-chemotherapy interaction analysis were utilized to examine clinical associations. RESULTS HN1 L exhibited upregulation in CRC, predominantly within tumor epithelial cells. Its overexpression augmented proliferation and migration, while knockdown induced the opposite effects. Endpoint xenograft outcomes and Ki-67 staining further corroborated its tumor-promoting role in vivo . Mechanistically, HN1 L diminished MOB1 and YAP phosphorylation, particularly at YAP Ser127 and Ser397, while elevating SNAIL expression, with overall YAP levels remaining largely unchanged. In the clinical cohort, baseline characteristics were generally consistent between HN1 L -high and HN1 L -low groups. High HN1 L expression correlated with reduced five-year overall survival (60% 95%CI: 34%-100% vs 96% 95%CI: 87%-100%, log-rank P = 0.039). Among HN1 L-high patients, the five-year disease-free survival (DFS) was 92% with adjuvant chemotherapy compared to 52% without. A significant HN1 L -by-chemotherapy interaction was noted for DFS (interaction hazard ratio = 0.09, 95%CI: 0.008-0.901; P = 0.031). CONCLUSION HN1 L promotes CRC progression by suppressing Hippo pathway activity. Elevated HN1 L expression correlates with poorer clinical outcomes and differential adjuvant chemotherapy benefit in this retrospective cohort, thereby supporting its potential role in CRC risk stratification and treatment selection.

title: Development and internal validation of a disease-free survival model after radical resection of pathological T4 colorectal adenocarcinoma
abstractText: BACKGROUND Postoperative outcomes vary substantially among patients with pathological T4 (pT4) colorectal adenocarcinoma despite radical resection. Pathological staging may not fully capture risk heterogeneity within this high-risk population. AIM To develop and internally validate a disease-free survival (DFS) prediction model after radical resection of pT4 colorectal adenocarcinoma. METHODS This single-center retrospective cohort included 440 of 690 patients screened from 2018 to 2022. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator-Cox regression was used for predictor selection, followed by unpenalized Cox refitting in the full cohort. Conditional optimism correction used 1000 bootstrap resamples with selected terms fixed. Apparent time-dependent discrimination, calibration, and decision curves were evaluated at 36 months and 60 months. A TNM-only Cox comparator based on pT4 subtype and pN stage was used. RESULTS During a median follow-up of 51 months, 159 patients (36.1%) experienced a DFS event. Seven clinical variables represented by eight regression terms were retained. The apparent concordance index was 0.670 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.628-0.711] and 0.652 after conditional optimism correction. Apparent time-dependent areas under the curve were 0.704 (95%CI: 0.650-0.756) at 36 months and 0.717 (95%CI: 0.644-0.780) at 60 months. The TNM-only comparator had apparent and conditional optimism-corrected C-indices of 0.609 and 0.598, respectively. Apparent calibration showed generally close agreement between predicted and observed risks, and decision curves suggested potential net benefit across portions of the evaluated threshold range. CONCLUSION The proposed model provided more detailed postoperative risk characterization than TNM staging alone, with moderate discrimination and reasonable apparent calibration. External validation is required before clinical use.

title: Forward model of the Gaia DR3 selection function
abstractText: The completeness of an astronomical catalogue depends on its selection function, which is a combination of the observing strategy, instrumental characteristics, and intrinsic properties of the sources being observed. This is particularly complex for Gaia, whose non-uniform scanning law and onboard prioritisation of bright sources in dense areas make its selection function vary strongly with celestial position and source brightness. We estimate the source catalogue selection function across the whole sky and over the full magnitude range, using only data from the Gaia catalogue and knowledge of the nominal scanning law as provided by the Gaia Observation Forecast Tool. 3 We developed a hierarchical Bayesian model that estimates the number of times Gaia scanned each celestial position jointly with the source detection efficiency, and fitted it via Markov chain Monte Carlo to the 1,806,196,447 sources in 3 with reported celestial positions, G magnitudes, and astrometric matched transit counts. 3 is essentially complete for G ∈ (5,19.5) in the on-sky median. After that, the completeness decreases with magnitude according to the scanning law pattern combined with the imprint of crowded regions. The completeness is also lower at the very bright end of the survey, consistent with the known limitations on Gaia observations of bright stars. We find an unexpected completeness increase beyond G ∼ 21, which we conclude is an artefact caused by extended sources, as confirmed by cross-matching against Euclid's Q1 catalogue. Our approach builds on previous efforts that use the understanding of the Gaia survey strategy to model the survey selection function. Our model does not rely on a precise knowledge of the Gaia scanning law, making it more robust, while retaining the capability of deriving an all-sky selection function without the need to extrapolate from limited external surveys providing `ground truth'. Treating the scanning law as part of the inference process, and anchoring it to all sources of all magnitudes on a fine-grained grid on the sky, removes the need for an explicit crowding correction. The resulting selection function, valid everywhere where Gaia data are available, is released as part of the GaiaUnlimited Python package. 3

title: Autonomic neural reprogramming in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma: Putative neurotumoral circuits linking perineural invasion to metastatic progression
abstractText: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a highly lethal gastrointestinal malignancy characterized by dense neural innervation and a pronounced tendency for perineural infiltration, pathological features closely associated with poor prognosis and metastatic spread. Recent studies support a model of PDAC as a neurotropic malignant tumor potentially associated with a self-reinforcing autonomic-neural-tumor network-in which sympathetic components, tumor cells, and stromal fibroblasts form an integrated neuro-oncologic network that may contribute to tumor invasiveness, microenvironment adaptation, and metastatic potential. However, evidence for spontaneous distant metastasis and clinically meaningful therapeutic benefit remains limited. This narrative review aims to examine the neuro-oncologic interface in PDAC, focusing on the sympathetic nerve-cancer associated fibroblasts feedback loop model and the PIEZO1-YAP1 mechanotransduction axis, and to discuss how these pathways may contribute to perineural invasion and systemic dissemination, thereby highlighting a potential novel therapeutic strategy.

title: Spatial macrophage signatures and prognostic relevance of NFKB1 in colorectal cancer
abstractText: BACKGROUND Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) exhibit substantial spatial and transcriptional heterogeneity in colorectal cancer (CRC). However, the prognostic relevance of spatial macrophage-associated transcriptional programs remains incompletely understood. AIM To characterize spatial macrophage-associated transcriptional programs and evaluate the prognostic relevance of NFKB1 in CRC. METHODS A publicly available conventional 10x Genomics Visium FFPE colorectal cancer specimen was integrated with The Cancer Genome Atlas colon adenocarcinoma cohort and external Gene Expression Omnibus bulk-transcriptomic cohorts. Spatial M1-like and M2-like macrophage-associated transcriptional-program activity was quantified using AUCell, whereas the corresponding bulk-cohort signature scores were calculated using single-sample gene set enrichment analysis. Candidate genes were prioritized using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator Cox regression and other survival-learning methods. Subsequently, the associations of NFKB1 with survival, clinicopathological characteristics, immune-related transcriptional features, representative protein staining, pathway enrichment, and predicted drug responses were evaluated. RESULTS Spatial distribution analysis revealed distinct structural characteristics of different compartments within the tumor immune system. The activity of an M2-like macrophage-associated signature was greater in tumor-core, invasive-front, and stroma-enriched regions, whereas the activity of an M1-like macrophage-associated signature was higher at tumor-peripheral regions and in areas at tumor-normal interfaces. Higher M1-like scores were correlated with early tumor stage and better overall survival (OS). The assessed prognostic models showed moderate discrimination (the best mean time-dependent area under the curve was 0.650). NFKB1 was prioritized as a candidate gene associated with the M1-like signature. In selected external cohorts, higher NFKB1 expression was associated with improved OS and correlated with transcriptional features characteristic of immune-active states. Differences in predicted drug response values were observed between the NFKB1 -high and NFKB1 -low groups. CONCLUSION M1- and M2-like macrophage-associated transcriptional programs showed distinct spatial distributions in colorectal cancer. Higher M1-like signature activity was preferentially observed in tumor-peripheral regions and was associated with immune-active features and more favorable survival. NFKB1 expression was also associated with the M1-like program and favorable outcomes in selected external cohorts. These findings support NFKB1 as a candidate bulk-transcriptomic biomarker.

title: Association of one-year postoperative patient-reported outcomes with recurrence and survival in stage I non-small-cell lung cancer
abstractText: BACKGROUND Recurrence risk and overall survival (OS) after curative-intent resection for stage I non-small-cell lung cancer remain incompletely explained by tumor-related variables. Patient-reported outcomes may capture dimensions of postoperative health not represented by conventional clinicopathologic factors, but their prognostic role during survivorship remains insufficiently defined. AIM To determine whether patient-reported outcomes assessed 1 year after surgery are associated with subsequent recurrence and OS. METHODS We analyzed 349 consecutive patients undergoing resection for pathological stage I non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) between 2006 and 2018. The 1-year landmark cohort comprised 232 patients alive and recurrence-free with available health-related quality of life data. Global health status (QL2), fatigue (FA), and dyspnea (DY) from the European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire-Core 30 were evaluated. Recurrence was the primary endpoint, with death treated as a competing event. Multivariable recurrence analyses used cause-specific Firth Cox and Fine-Gray models; OS was assessed using multivariable Firth Cox regression. RESULTS During follow-up, 35 patients (15.1%) developed recurrence and 15 (6.5%) died without prior relapse. Age ≥ 65 years [hazard ratio (HR) = 6.51, 95%CI: 2.37-17.90], higher QL2 (HR = 2.50, 95%CI: 1.15-5.40), and higher FA (HR = 3.48, 95%CI: 1.66-7.27) were independently associated with recurrence, whereas DY was inversely associated (HR = 0.33, 95%CI: 0.16-0.71). Fine-Gray models yielded consistent estimates. For OS, age ≥ 65 years (HR = 4.90, 95%CI: 1.19-20.05) and DY > 0 (HR = 0.26, 95%CI: 0.09-0.81) were independently associated with mortality, whereas FA ≥ 22.2 showed a clinically relevant but borderline association (HR = 2.94, 95%CI: 0.96-9.02). Model discrimination was good for recurrence (C-index 0.79) and OS (C-index 0.73). CONCLUSION Postoperative patient-reported outcomes assessed at 1 year were associated with heterogeneous recurrence and survival trajectories, suggesting complementary prognostic information during survivorship after stage I NSCLC resection.
