title: Strategi Pemanfaatan Media Sosial Instagram Komisi Pemilihan Umum Kabupaten Bandung Barat dalam Meningkatkan Pengetahuan Pemilih
abstractText: Dominasi pemilih muda dalam pemilihan umum menuntut lembaga penyelenggara pemilu untuk menyesuaikan strategi komunikasi politiknya ke ruang digital. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis strategi pemanfaatan media sosial Instagram oleh Komisi Pemilihan Umum (KPU) Kabupaten Bandung Barat dalam meningkatkan pengetahuan pemilih, serta mengidentifikasi hambatan dan tantangan dalam pelaksanaannya. Menggunakan paradigma konstruktivisme, pendekatan kualitatif, dan metode studi kasus, data dikumpulkan melalui wawancara semi-terstruktur terhadap empat pegawai internal KPU dan dua pemilih Generasi Z, disertai observasi langsung serta dokumentasi. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa pemanfaatan Instagram dilaksanakan melalui tiga tahapan terpadu: perencanaan (penetapan tujuan edukasi, penentuan sasaran pemilih pemula dan pemilih muda, serta sinergi dengan sosialisasi konvensional), implementasi (optimalisasi fitur Feed, Story, Carousel, dan Reels melalui penyederhanaan bahasa serta penyajian visual), dan evaluasi (pemantauan Instagram Insight serta respons komentar audiens untuk perbaikan konten). Hambatan utama meliputi rendahnya minat masyarakat terhadap konten edukasi dibandingkan hiburan, keterbatasan sumber daya manusia dengan keterampilan teknis yang beragam, derasnya arus informasi digital, serta penyebaran hoaks. Tantangan tersebut diatasi melalui evaluasi konten berkelanjutan, adaptasi tren tanpa mengurangi substansi kepemiluan, penyederhanaan visual, dan penguatan koordinasi internal. Penelitian ini berkontribusi pada praktik komunikasi politik digital dengan menunjukkan bagaimana penyelenggara pemilu tingkat daerah menyeimbangkan kredibilitas kelembagaan dengan pendidikan pemilih yang adaptif terhadap karakteristik platform.

title: Study on multi-field coupling characteristics and performance of reciprocating seals in landing gear actuators
abstractText: Purpose This study aims to address the frequent seal failure issue of aircraft landing gear actuators, focusing on the complex service conditions involving wide temperature ranges and real-time variations in reciprocating speed. By taking a typical T-shaped seal ring as the research object, this work seeks to reveal the intrinsic mechanism of sealing performance degradation. Design/methodology/approach A fluid-solid-thermal coupled mixed lubrication model is established via finite element analysis and numerical calculation methods. The model is used to investigate the effects of pressure, temperature and reciprocating speed on sealing performance, and its reliability is further validated through bench tests. Findings The results demonstrate pressure and temperature exert significant regulatory effects on sealing performance. Specifically, the leakage rate abruptly increases at 45 MPa, indicating a system-specific leakage-instability threshold. The friction force during the internal stroke is sensitive to pressure and temperature, whereas the external stroke friction force shows low sensitivity to these operating parameters. Additionally, with increasing temperature, both internal and external stroke friction forces decrease while the leakage rate increases. Bench test results confirm that the error of the measured leakage rate is within 10%, verifying the reliability of the proposed model. Originality/value This study establishes a multi-field coupled model for T-shaped seal rings under complex service conditions, providing a theoretical basis for improving the sealing reliability of landing gear actuators.

title: Analisis Perencanaan Karir dan Lingkungan Kerja terhadap Retensi Karyawan Generasi Z: Studi Kasus pada Krakatau Steel
abstractText: Keberhasilan suatu perusahaan tidak terlepas dari peran sumber daya manusia yang ada di dalamnya. Bisa dibuat lebih mengalir dan natural seperti ini. Seiring semakin banyaknya Generasi Z yang memasuki dunia kerja, perusahaan perlu memahami berbagai faktor yang dapat membuat karyawan merasa nyaman dan memilih untuk tetap bertahan. Oleh karena itu, penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis peran perencanaan karier dan lingkungan kerja terhadap retensi karyawan Generasi Z di PT Krakatau Steel. Metode yang digunakan adalah kualitatif deskriptif dengan pendekatan studi pustaka melalui jurnal, buku, dan dokumen perusahaan. Hasil kajian menunjukkan bahwa kejelasan jenjang karir, kesempatan pengembangan diri, serta lingkungan kerja yang aman dan nyaman dapat mendorong karyawan untuk bertahan di perusahaan. Oleh karena itu, kedua faktor tersebut perlu diperhatikan dalam mempertahankan karyawan Generasi Z.

title: AI words, AI deeds, and environmental assessment: the role of managerial ability
abstractText: Purpose This study aims to examine how managerial ability (MA), AI-related disclosure (AI Words) and AI-related investment intensity (AI Deeds), a CSMAR-based proxy covering enabling digital assets, relate to composite environmental performance (EP) and external environmental ratings and whether the two AI measures are assessed differently. Design/methodology/approach Using data from Chinese non-financial A-share listed firms for 2010–2023, the study estimates models with firm and year fixed effects to examine the associations of MA, AI Words and AI Deeds with EP and external environmental ratings. Findings MA has a modest positive association with EP and a consistent negative association with AI Deeds, although the corresponding indirect association remains exploratory. In the contemporaneous model for the full rated sample, AI Words is associated with higher external ratings and AI Deeds with lower ratings, while neither is associated with rating-excluded EP. This pattern indicates a potential environmental assessment gap. Practical implications Regulators, rating providers and boards may benefit from distinguishing visible AI narratives from verifiable implementation and outcomes. Assessment and oversight frameworks for climate-transition governance could consider disclosure, resource allocation and energy implications rather than treating AI adoption as uniformly beneficial. Such alignment may also strengthen the credibility of sustainability information, stakeholder trust and corporate accountability. Originality/value Building on words–deeds, symbolic–substantive and AI-washing research, this study extends the words–deeds distinction to environmental assessment and positions MA as a governance-related resource-orchestration factor while recognising the measurement sensitivity of the MA–EP evidence.

title: Lived Experiences and Challenges of the Volunteer Probation Assistants in Community-Based Corrections: A Phenomenological Study in Nueva Vizcaya, Philippines
abstractText: This study explored the lived experiences of Volunteer Probation Assistants (VPAs) in Nueva Vizcaya while providing assistance in the rehabilitation and supervision of clients in the community. Using a qualitative phenomenological design, participants were purposively selected from the VPAs in the province of Nueva Vizcaya. Data were gathered through in-depth interviews utilizing a semi-structured interview guide, with the responses transcribed, translated, and analyzed using thematic analysis. Findings revealed that participants experienced their volunteer work through their commitment to guiding and supporting clients, fulfillment in providing assistance and opportunities for clients, personal and professional growth, and joy in witnessing clients’ positive transformation, while also encountering sadness and grief over the death of an assigned client. The study also identified various challenges encountered by VPAs, which include dealing with client-related difficulties, safety and security concerns during home visitation, supervision difficulties of clients residing in far municipalities, financial limitations, and difficulty in tracing new probationers. Thus, the study emphasized the significant role and meaningful contributions of the VPAs in community-based rehabilitation, specifically in the successful reintegration and rehabilitation of clients in the community. The findings serve as the basis for developing an intervention program aimed at addressing the identified challenges and enhancing the support programs for VPAs

title: Machine learning based prediction of tensile strength properties of fused filament fabricated PA-CFRP composites
abstractText: Purpose Fused filament fabrication (FFF) has gained substantial attention in additive manufacturing for making lightweight functional structural components. However, the mechanical performance of FFF-fabricated parts is heavily impacted by several interdependent processing parameters, making accurate prediction challenging. This study aims to establish a precise machine learning-based framework to forecast the tensile characteristics of polyamide–carbon fiber reinforced polymer composites made using the FFF technique. Design/methodology/approach A thorough experimental data set was developed by systematically adjusting key FFF processing parameters, including nozzle temperature, layer height, infill density, printing speed and infill pattern. Machine learning models, particularly random forest, Extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) and Light gradient boosting machine (GBM), were created to predict tensile strength, Young’s modulus and elongation at break. Model performance was evaluated using the coefficient of determination (R2), and feature importance analysis was conducted to determine the most relevant process parameters. Findings Among the examined models, XGBoost had the highest predictive accuracy, reaching R2 values of 0.998 for the training data set and 0.956 for the test data set. LightGBM displayed greater generalization ability for all three mechanical properties. The five-fold cross validation showed mean R2 values of 0.921 for ultimate tensile strength, 0.871 for Young’s modulus and 0.889 for elongation demonstrating the robustness of the models. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis indicated layer height as the most important parameter, followed by nozzle temperature and infill density. Originality/value This research includes various steps such as mechanical property prediction based on data, automatic hyperparameters optimization using Optuna, comparison of various machine learning models, multi-objective optimization by means of NSGA-III and explanation of the artificial intelligence model by SHAP. The suggested method markedly diminishes experimental workload and material wastage, offering a rapid and efficient instrument for optimizing processes and predicting mechanical properties in additive manufacturing.

title: Evaluation of black soldier fly fats as biolubricant additives: influence of developmental stage on tribological performance
abstractText: Purpose This study aims to evaluate unmodified fats from fifth-instar larvae and prepupae of black soldier fly (Hermetia illucens) reared on food waste as biolubricant additives in 150N mineral oil and compares their oxidation stability and tribological performance. Design/methodology/approach The fats were added directly to mineral oil without chemical modification. Their thermal and oxidation stability was characterized, while their tribological performance was evaluated using point-on-flat and point-to-point tests. The effects of additive concentration and temperature were examined under point-on-flat contact. Trimethylolpropane trioleate served as a commercial ester reference in the tribological tests. Worn surfaces were analyzed by optical profilometry and spectroscopy. Findings Prepupal fat had higher oxidation stability, whereas larval fat provided better friction reduction and wear protection. At 1 Wt.%, both fats reduced friction across the tested temperatures and outperformed the reference ester in wear protection. Larval fat performed best, reducing the friction coefficient by up to 25.97% and the wear rate by 96.63% in point-on-flat tests and 88.80% in point-to-point tests relative to the base oil. Surface analyses indicated protective film formation, consistent with the previously reported higher unsaturation of larval fat. Originality/value This study demonstrates the direct use of unmodified BSF fats as biolubricant additives at low concentrations and indicates that developmental stage may influence their suitability for lubrication applications.

title: Enhancing user engagement: a usability study of Ghanaian university library websites for improved accessibility and navigation
abstractText: Purpose This study aims to examine the usability of Ghanaian university library websites and its influence on user engagement, focusing on three key factors: accessibility, navigation and usability. Design/methodology/approach This study used a quantitative cross-sectional research design. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire informed by the technology acceptance model (TAM) and Nielsen’s usability heuristics. This study involved 340 library users from five purposively selected public universities in Ghana. Participants were recruited using convenience sampling. Data were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling. Findings The results revealed that accessibility and navigation had significant positive effects on user engagement, with accessibility emerging as the strongest predictor (β = 0.352, t = 5.412, p < 0.001). Navigation also had a significant positive effect on user engagement (β = 0.191, t = 2.856, p = 0.004). Although usability had a positive relationship with user engagement, its effect was not statistically significant at the 5% significance level (β = 0.112, t = 1.920, p = 0.055). The model explained 53.3% of the variance in website user engagement. Research limitations/implications A key limitation of this study is its focus on academic library websites in Ghana, which may limit the generalizability of findings to other developing countries or regions with differing socio-economic and technological contexts. In addition, the study relied primarily on self-reported data from questionnaires, which may be subject to respondent bias, such as over- or under-reporting of experiences. The exclusion of longitudinal analysis means that the study does not capture changes in usability and engagement over time. Furthermore, resource constraints limited the sample size of administrators and Web developers, potentially restricting the depth of insights into the technical challenges faced in maintaining academic library websites. Future research could address these limitations by using a longitudinal approach, expanding the geographical scope and incorporating additional qualitative methods, such as focus groups or observational studies, to gain a deeper understanding of user behaviour and website usability. Originality/value This study provides empirical evidence on the factors influencing engagement with Ghanaian university library websites and demonstrates the importance of accessibility and navigation in website development and evaluation. The findings highlight the need for user-centred website design, adherence to established Web accessibility standards such as the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines, mobile-responsive design and regular usability evaluation. These measures can support more effective access to library resources and services, particularly within resource-constrained university environments.

title: Artificial intelligence and the future of youth employment in a developing economy: skills mismatch, early-career transitions and labour market vulnerability
abstractText: Purpose This study aims to examine how artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping youth employment in Morocco, focusing on labour market vulnerability, skills mismatch and early-career transitions. Design/methodology/approach This study adopts a mixed-methods approach combining a task-based quantitative analysis of secondary labour market data with qualitative evidence from 12 semi-structured expert interviews. Findings The findings indicate that AI adoption in Morocco remains limited and uneven, with applications concentrated mainly on basic functions. The quantitative analysis highlights the structural characteristics of youth employment, while the interviews reveal concerns about skills mismatch, access to early-career opportunities and potential AI-related job displacement. A central finding is the youth paradox: young people are perceived as digitally adaptable but continue to face structural barriers to quality employment and AI-complementary opportunities. The findings also highlight the importance of education and skills development, stronger school-to-work transition mechanisms and institutional coordination in supporting inclusive adaptation to technological change. Originality/value Despite growing concern about AI’s labour-market implications, youth remain underrepresented in the literature, particularly in developing economies. Drawing on the routine-biased technological change and skill-biased technological change perspectives, the study explains how technological change interacts with labour-market structures and institutions to shape youth vulnerability. It further proposes a three-pillar AI adaptation framework centred on education and skills transformation, labour-market transition mechanisms and institutional and ecosystem capacity.

title: Mobile low-dose computed tomography lung cancer screening within an integrated thoracic oncology network: a real-world implementation and provider-cost evaluation
abstractText: To evaluate the clinical, operational, and economic performance of a community-based mobile low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) lung cancer screening program integrated with a tertiary thoracic oncology network. This retrospective implementation study included 1279 individuals screened in Milan, Italy, during November and December 2024. Among 250 screen-positive participants, initial management comprised immediate diagnostic evaluation or planned imaging surveillance - an exploratory logistic regression examined factors associated with immediate diagnostic allocation. A provider-cost scenario model applied assumed annual fixed costs and a constant variable cost per scan to alternative annual screening volumes. Overall, 250 participants (19.5%) had at least one nodule measuring 6 mm or more, and 52 (4.1%) entered the immediate diagnostic pathway. Five lung cancers were detected, corresponding to a cancer detection rate of 0.39% [95% exact confidence interval (CI) = 0.13-0.91]. Nodule diameter and solid morphology were independently associated with diagnostic allocation; apparent model discrimination was 0.84 (95% CI = 0.80-0.88). The median interval from screening LDCT to the first recorded diagnostic assessment was 18 days. Modeled provider cost was approximately €391 per scan at an assumed annual volume of 1279 examinations and decreased in higher-volume scenarios. Mobile lung cancer screening can be integrated with specialist diagnostic pathways, but screening yield, participant selection, and program volume are central to its clinical and economic performance. The cost estimates depend on assumed annual throughput and do not establish cost-effectiveness.

title: Peran Guru PKN dalam Mengimplementasi Sila “Kemanusiaan yang Adil dan Beradab” kepada Siswa di SMP PGRI 3 PAGA

This study used a qualitative case study type approach with subjects namely PGRI 3 Paga middle school students. Data collection techniques used observation, documentation and interview data. Based on the results of the study it can be concluded that the role of PKN teachers in implementing just and civilized human precepts at SMP PGRI 3 Paga is based on the characteristics of students of different background, religions, ethnicities and so on in the form of mutual respect between religions by discriminating against students from different background his beliefs. PGRI 3 Paga middle school students already have a good understanding of just and civilized human precepts. Factors that support and hinder the role of PKN teachers in implementing just and civilized humanity precepts at SMP PGRI 3 Paga there are factors in the condition of children and families that are less supportive in implementing just and civilized humanitarian precepts the lack of time available for PKN lessons. The effect of green event on environmental loyalty: moderating role of organisers' green consciousness
abstractText: Purpose This study assesses how organisers’ green consciousness influences the effect of green events on environmental loyalty among event-organising firms in Ghana. Design/methodology/approach The study employed a cross-sectional survey design, soliciting data from 300 managers/owners of event-organising firms. The data were analysed using the PROCESS MACRO in SPSS v. 23 to help estimate the conditional relationships under the study. Findings The findings show that while green events significantly influenced environmental loyalty, organisers’ green consciousness further strengthened their effectiveness in encouraging environmental loyalty. Furthermore, dimensions of green events, such as green prices and green internal practices, had significant positive effects on environmental loyalty. Finally, organisers green consciousness significantly moderated the links between green experience, price, promotion, internal practices and environmental loyalty. Research limitations/implications Firstly, the study focused on event-organising firms in Ghana, which may limit the generalisability of the findings to other industries or geographical contexts. Secondly, the study's cross-sectional design limits the ability to infer causality between variables. Practical implications Consequently, to ensure a strong environmental loyalty to achieve sustainable development, there is the need for policy makers and event organisations to encourage green practices and events, as well as promote green awareness among event organisers to strengthen their consciousness. Originality/value The novelty of this study lies in its contribution to the green event and environmental loyalty literature, potentially as one of the first to advance the value–belief–norm (VBN) theory in this context.

Assessing the Effectiveness of Machine Learning Models in Predicting the Target Properties of Modified Pervious Concrete Mixtures
abstractText: Pervious concrete (PC) serves as a highly porous pavement material enabling water infiltration, stormwater runoff reduction, and groundwater recharge. PC properties are often governed by factors such as aggregate shape, size, and pore characteristics, cement content, water–cement ratio, and additives. Although machine learning (ML) has transformed the construction industry by predicting conventional concrete properties, studies on PC with additives remain limited. Thus, the major objective of this study was to assess the effectiveness of ML models and algorithms in predicting the target properties of PC mixtures, including compressive strength (CS), porosity, and permeability, based on random forest (RF), gradient boosting (GB), and artificial neural network (ANN) using a master database of 350 data points covering 78 mixtures. An independent 36-point external validation set was used to assess model generalizability. The input parameters used for developing the models included water-to-cement ratio, aggregate-to-cement (a/c) ratio, density, and additives such as silica fume and crumb rubber. Performance metrics indicated that RF and GB outperformed ANN during CS prediction, with test coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.79 and 0.80, and root mean square error of 2.04 and 1.97 MPa, respectively. Further, mixture-level out-of-fold R2 of 0.45 (RF) and 0.44 (GB) represented the unbiased estimates. All three models predicted porosity and permeability with good to excellent accuracy (R2 = 0.83–0.98). Furthermore, SHapley Additive exPlanations-based feature importance analysis revealed that density dominated CS prediction, and the a/c ratio governed porosity and permeability, thereby corroborating the distinct physical mechanisms controlling the mechanical and hydraulic performance of PC. All three ML models predicted the target PC properties with very good to excellent accuracy; however, the RF model showed the narrowest expected difference range (d3s) for predicted PC properties. It is envisioned that the proposed algorithms in this study can be readily applied in practice by entering component quantities in the same format as the training dataset. Overall, this research study contributed to comprehending the PC properties better and will serve as the foundation for a computational and statistical framework in the future to facilitate a paradigm shift toward developing environmentally sustainable and resilient roadway infrastructure materials/systems.

title: Parental influence and university choice: a marketing mix perspective from private higher education in Bangladesh
abstractText: Purpose In cultures with strong familial values, parents play a crucial role in shaping students’ educational choices. In the higher education context, understanding the factors influencing students’ university selection is essential. This study aims to examine the impact of parental influence and the marketing mix on students’ decision-making when choosing private higher education institutions in Bangladesh. Although marketing mix theory, social cognitive career theory (SCCT) and cultural capital theory have each informed research on university choice separately, their combined application to explain gendered, family-mediated decision-making in a collectivist developing-country context remains largely unexamined. Design/methodology/approach Grounded in SCCT, cultural capital theory and the 7Ps marketing mix framework, this study adopts a quantitative approach using data from 298 students attending private higher education institutions in Bangladesh, analysed through partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) with measurement invariance, multi-group analysis and effect-size (f2, Q2) assessment. Findings The findings identify parental influence as the key determinant in university choice, particularly for female students. Female students tend to rely more on family guidance when evaluating educational quality and tuition fees, whereas male students are more independent in assessing academic programmes and financial considerations. The results also indicate that the location of the university is the least significant factor affecting students’ choices. Research limitations/implications The findings highlight the importance of incorporating socio-cultural factors, particularly parental influence, when applying the marketing mix framework in collectivist societies. The results suggest that universities should prioritise parental engagement, academic quality and campus resources in their marketing strategies rather than focusing primarily on institutional location. Originality/value Rather than treating parental influence as a uniform mediator, this study shows that it selectively transmits the effects of tangible and verifiable marketing cues, including product quality, price and physical infrastructure. Experiential cues such as people, process and promotion remain largely unmediated. Drawing on Bourdieu’s distinction between objectified and embodied cultural capital and SCCT’s proximal and distal framework, this study provides empirical evidence on which institutional marketing signals are subject to parental gatekeeping in a collectivist and gender-differentiated context. It also provides a joint test of SCCT, cultural capital theory and the 7Ps within a single mediation and moderation PLS-SEM model in South Asian private higher education.

title: Networked impact: donor contribution visualization, relational embeddedness, and blood donor citizenship behavior intention
abstractText: Purpose This paper examines how donor contribution network visualization, supported by traceable digital infrastructure, influences blood donor citizenship behavior intention. Design/methodology/approach Three studies were conducted. Study 1 used a scenario-based online experiment to test the effect of donor contribution network visualization on blood donor citizenship behavior intention. Study 2 used a field experiment in a provincial blood center to examine the indirect pathway through relational embeddedness. Study 3 tested the moderating role of information framing (collectivism vs. individualism). Findings Donor contribution network visualization increases blood donor citizenship behavior intention. The results reveal a significant indirect effect through relational embeddedness, and additional analyses yielded no significant indirect effects through warm glow, perceived donation impact, or perceived relationship investment. The positive effect of visualization on relational embeddedness and its indirect effect on blood donor citizenship behavior intention are stronger under collectivism framing than under individualism framing. Originality/value This paper conceptualizes donor contribution network visualization as a self-anchored, donor-facing visualization-based feedback mechanism for prosocial service engagement. Its novelty lies in making the focal donor's own networked contribution visible and relationally interpretable. The study extends social exchange theory to digitally mediated altruistic contexts, highlights relational embeddedness as a key relational pathway and identifies information framing as a boundary condition consistent with interface–message fit.

title: Evaluation of the rbcL gene as a DNA barcode marker for accurate identification of Baccaurea species in Riau, Indonesia
abstractText: Accurate identification of Baccaurea species is challenged by morphological similarities among taxa. This study evaluates the rbcL gene as DNA barcode for Baccaurea species in Riau, Indonesia. A total of 50 specimens, encompassing seven morphologically verified species, underwent DNA extraction using a modified CTAB protocol, followed by PCR amplification and sequencing of the rbcL region. Amplification was universally successful (100%), while sequencing success was high, except for B. bracteata. The presence of a conspicuous DNA barcode gap, with the minimum interspecific distance (0.002) exceeding the maximum intraspecific distance (0.000), indicating measurable genetic differentiation among sampled taxa. Phylogenetic reconstruction using the Neighbor-Joining method produced distinct clustering patterns and supported overall taxonomic structure. However, BLAST and BOLD analyses confirmed reliable genus-level assignments, while species-level resolution remained limited. These results demonstrate that rbcL provides a robust molecular baseline for genus-level identification and phylogenetic assessment in Baccaurea, although additional markers may be required to achieve consistent species-level discrimination.

Exploring the Impact of Lactobacillus plantarum B1765 Fermentation on the Chemical Characteristics and Antioxidant Potential of Gembili (Dioscorea esculenta) Flour
abstractText: Gembili (Dioscorea esculenta) is an underutilized tuber with potential as a functional food ingredient due to its bioactive compounds, particularly phenolics, which contribute to antioxidant activity. Fermentation using lactic acid bacteria offers an approach to enhance its functional properties. This study aimed to investigate the effects of fermentation using Lactobacillus plantarum B1765 on the physicochemical characteristics, total phenolic content (TPC), and antioxidant activity of gembili flour. Gembili tubers were fermented for 0, 2, 4, and 6 days using 3% (v/v) L. plantarum B1765 starter culture at 37°C. The fermented tubers were oven-dried at 50°C, ground, and sieved through an 80-mesh sieve. The parameters Analysed included pH, total titratable acidity (TTA), moisture content, TPC, and antioxidant activity using the DPPH assay. 30 untrained panelists also conducted organoleptic evaluation. Data were Analysed using one-way ANOVA followed by post hoc LSD testing at p<0.05. The results showed that fermentation increased TPC from 33,83 to 146,94 mg GAE/g extract and enhanced antioxidant activity, as indicated by a decrease in IC?? from 193,67 to 15,21 ppm after 6 days. Moisture content decreased from 12,32% to 5,28%, accompanied by changes in pH and TTA. Organoleptic acceptance also improved, with the highest scores for color and texture observed after 6 days, while aroma acceptance increased until day 4. These findings indicate that fermentation with L. plantarum B1765 can improve the chemical and antioxidant properties of gembili flour. title: Contextualized Mathematics for Productive Work: Enhancing Numeracy and Employability Skills in The Alternative Learning System
abstractText: This research assessed the work approaches and academic performance in Mathematics of the ALS JHS learners in Danao City Division, Bohol Province Division, Region 7 and Leyte Province Division , Region 8 for SY 2024-2025 as basis for the Productive Work Plan. This study used the descriptive-correlational design with a total respondent of 64 of whom are 4 teachers and 60 ALS students having four Community Learning Centers. The demographic characteristics of teachers reflect their professional maturity, educational qualifications, and experience in handling ALS students. Conversely, the learners’ demographic profile offers insight into their learning readiness, motivational sources, and environmental support systems. The significance values presented in this section offer quantitative evidence of these relationships. A significant correlation (denoted by p < 0.05 or p < 0.01) implies that learners who demonstrate stronger positive work attitudes tend to perform better in mathematics, while a non-significant relationship (p > 0.05) indicates that the association is not strong enough to assert a consistent effect. Collectively, the results reflect that positive work attitudes contribute meaningfully to higher mathematical achievement, particularly in cognitively demanding areas. This relationship pattern also emphasizes that Mathematics achievement in ALS is not purely a matter of cognitive ability but rather a combination of emotional readiness, mindset, and instructional design. Teachers play a crucial role in sustaining motivation and enjoyment by making lessons meaningful and relevant to real-life applications. The learners’ strong attitudinal disposition indicates potential, but without adequate scaffolding, the link between mindset and mastery may weaken. Based on the conclusions reached in this research, it is highly recommended that appropriate Productive Work Approaches and Math Performance Integrative Instructional Plan for all schools in the Division of City of Danao, Bantayan Island, Cebu Province, Inabanga District, Cebu Province and Tabango Leyte Province be considered for implementation.

title: A Study on Ethical Dilemmas in Tsunami Evacuation Using a Margin Time Approach
abstractText: Stopover behavior, such as checking on family members, assisting neighbors, or gathering information, frequently delayed tsunami evacuation and increased fatality risk during the 2011 Great East Japan Earthquake. Rooted in relational responsibility and cultural norms, such behavior creates an ethical dilemma under severe time constraints, yet existing research lacks a rigorous framework for identifying where and to what extent these delays become life-threatening. Focusing on the Taro district of Miyako City and Rikuzentakata City in Iwate Prefecture, this study builds pedestrian evacuation networks from publicly available geospatial data, including maximum-class tsunami inundation scenarios, minimum tsunami arrival times, coastlines, road networks, and a 1-meter-mesh digital elevation model. We define the evacuation time margin as Margin = TArrival − (TWalk + TStopover) and classify each location as Red (evacuation infeasible), Yellow (feasible only without delay), or Green (sufficient margin), with unroutable points treated as Gray. The Yellow zone, termed the Ethical Dilemma Band (EDB), marks where brief hesitation can determine survival. Walking-speed and slope-dependent sensitivity analyses further test how EDBs expand across stopover durations. In Taro, the area is almost entirely safe under immediate evacuation, with the Yellow zone negligible at a 5-minute stopover but expanding non-linearly from about 10 minutes onward. Rikuzentakata shows persistent coastal Red zones and a wide Yellow expansion beginning as early as 5 minutes. Slower walking enlarges the Yellow zone in both regions, while slope correction additionally produces new Red cells in steep Taro and expands the existing Red zone in Rikuzentakata. Ethical dilemmas thus arise from temporal structures shaped by topography and road networks. The study introduces ethics as spatial structure, places time-creating (+Margin) and delay-reducing (−Stopover) measures on a shared temporal scale, and shows that EDB expansion is region-specific, supporting evacuation planning tailored to local conditions.

title: Degradation of Drugs of Abuse and Associated Microbial Community Shifts in Freshwater Systems
abstractText: Drugs of abuse (DAs) are frequently detected in surface waters due to their incomplete removal during wastewater treatment and continued discharge from point and nonpoint sources. Despite growing evidence of ecological effects at environmentally relevant concentrations, the environmental fate of many DAs in river systems remains insufficiently characterized. In this study, we evaluated the degradation of eight commonly detected DAs and metabolites (amphetamine, benzoylecgonine, buprenorphine, codeine, fentanyl, ketamine, methamphetamine, and tramadol) spiked at environmentally relevant concentrations in river microcosms designed to distinguish hydrolysis, abiotic degradation, biodegradation, and sorption processes. Microcosms were incubated under dark, aerobic conditions for 9 days, and first-order kinetics were used to quantify individual degradation rate constants. Overall removal was limited, ranging from 12% (tramadol) to 21% (buprenorphine), indicating high persistence under the microcosm conditions. Hydrolysis and abiotic degradation contributed minimally to attenuation, whereas biodegradation accounted for the largest estimated contribution (k = 0.0044–0.016 d–1), with sorption providing a secondary estimated contribution for more hydrophobic compounds. Principal component analysis indicated that attenuation behavior was associated with physicochemical properties, including hydrophobicity and ionization; compounds such as buprenorphine and fentanyl showed stronger associations with sorption and hydrolysis, while ketamine attenuation was more strongly influenced by ionization than sorption. Parallel taxonomic analysis revealed temporal shifts in microbial community composition, although Pseudomonadota (formerly Proteobacteria) and Bacteroidota (formerly Bacteroidetes) remained dominant throughout the incubation. Dynamic community restructuring was observed in biologically active microcosms based on taxonomic profiling, although changes could not be linked directly to drug presence. Overall, degradation rates in river water were 1–4 orders of magnitude lower than those reported for wastewater or sludge matrices, suggesting greater persistence and prolonged ecological exposure in freshwater systems. These findings improve understanding of the environmental fate of DAs and support risk assessment efforts for bioactive contaminants in aquatic ecosystems.

title: Branding disconnection through nostalgia in digital detox tourism
abstractText: Purpose This study aims to examine how digital detox tourism brands use nostalgia to construct the emotional appeal and communicated experiential value of disconnection, and how these meanings are received and negotiated by participants and consumers. Design/methodology/approach The study combines a qualitative thematic content analysis of 73 brand-produced and brand-attributable promotional items from The Offline Club, Camp Grounded and Unplugged with a supplementary qualitative analysis of 28 publicly available first-person participant and consumer accounts. The analysis focuses on nostalgic cues, analogue practices, emotional framing and the relationship between branded meanings and public reception. Findings Across the three cases, nostalgia operates as more than a decorative aesthetic device. It provides a symbolic and temporal frame through which technological absence is associated with simplicity, presence, play, sociability and self-reconnection, while analogisation materialises these meanings through tangible objects, practices, aesthetics and rituals. The findings suggest that nostalgia performs a value-conversion function by reframing technological absence from potential deprivation into experiential enrichment. The reception analysis further shows that these meanings are selectively reproduced, reinterpreted and sometimes challenged. Analogue engagement is widespread across the cases, whereas explicitly nostalgic reception varies considerably. Research limitations/implications This study has several limitations. The supplementary reception analysis relies on 28 publicly available, self-selected participant and consumer accounts, which vary in source type and temporal coverage and cannot provide the depth obtainable through primary interviews, ethnography or longitudinal research. The promotional corpus was also bounded to materials collected between March and April 2025, limiting insight into seasonal or longer-term changes in brand communication. In addition, the study focuses on three purposively selected cases, so the findings should be understood in terms of analytical transferability. Finally, visual material could be reproduced only where formal publication permission was obtained. Practical implications The findings suggest that digital detox providers should frame disconnection as a positive experiential gain associated with presence, calm, intimacy, play and sensory engagement. Analogue objects and activities can support this positioning when they serve a clear experiential function and help structure offline time. Managers should also ensure consistency between nostalgic promotional imagery and the material delivery of the experience, since perceived gaps may weaken authenticity and satisfaction. Finally, because disconnection is often negotiated and externally supported, providers should consider clear offline rituals, reliable analogue resources, community-based formats and flexible participation options that make temporary disconnection easier to sustain. Social implications The findings invite a critical reflection on how digital disconnection is increasingly framed as a purchasable lifestyle experience. Nostalgic representations may idealise simplified or selectively imagined versions of analogue life, while access to retreats, cabins and organised offline experiences depends on resources such as time, money and mobility. This raises questions about inequality in who can benefit from commercially organised disconnection. The study also suggests that digital fatigue may be individualised when disconnection is presented mainly as a personal consumption solution, while broader structural pressures associated with platform-based hyperconnectivity remain unaddressed. Environmental implications also warrant further attention. Originality/value The study extends research on digital detox and nostalgia marketing by explaining how nostalgic meaning and analogisation work together in the symbolic construction of value around digital disconnection. It also shows that brand-promoted nostalgia does not translate uniformly into public experience, highlighting the negotiated relationship between branding discourse, analogue engagement and public reception.

title: Targeting platelet protein kinases: therapeutic advances, developments and opportunities
abstractText: Purpose of review Human platelets contain about 6000 distinct proteins, among them hundreds of serine/threonine/tyrosine (S/T/Y) protein kinases (PKs) and protein phosphatases, which regulate an extensive repertoire of phosphorylation sites. Although there is a clear need for novel platelet inhibitors that go beyond aspirin and ADP-receptor antagonists, clinically well-established protein kinase inhibitors have received little attention as possible new generation of platelet inhibitors. Recent findings Recent proteome data sets identified 191 ST-PKs and 24 Y-PKs (catalytic subunits) in human platelets. This protein kinase network controls both platelet activation and inhibitory pathways, and alterations may be important for diseases with platelet hyperactivation. Over the last 25 years, more than 100 selective and FDA-approved kinase inhibitors have entered clinical practice for a variety of cancers and inflammatory disorders. Apart from the newer Bruton's tyrosine kinase inhibitors, successful in the treatment of B-cell malignancies, most of the FDA-approved kinase inhibitors have not been systematically evaluated in platelets. Summary The data presented here suggest that certain protein kinase inhibitors, alone and especially in well-selected combinations, merit consideration as novel antiplatelet drugs. The existing protein kinase inhibitor toolbox is ready for further preclinical and clinical investigation in thrombo-inflammatory and malignant conditions driven by hyperactivated platelets.

Age-related complications associated with endovascular treatment of intracranial aneurysms: An ambispective cohort study
abstractText: Objective: To determine the incidence, severity and attribution of complications after endovascular treatment of intracranial aneurysms, and to compare patterns across pediatric, adult and older adult patients at two Egyptian centers. Methods: Ambispective cohort study. Of 427 patients treated between April 2019 and August 2024, 380 were eligible; 60 (15.8%) sustained at least one complication and constituted the complication cohort (67 aneurysms), stratified as pediatric (≤18 years, n=18), adult (19-49 years, n=15) and older adult (≥50 years, n=27). The 86 events were classified by severity and attribution. Incidence used the 380 eligible patients; comparisons used the complication cohort. With 17 outcome events, multivariable analysis was limited to two covariates. Results: Complication incidence was 15.8%, major complication with neurological deficit 4.5% and in-hospital mortality 1.6%. Of 17 major neurological complications, 4 were procedure-attributable (1.1% of 380) and 13 disease-attributable (3.4%). Across strata, all-cause major neurological complications occurred in 22.2%, 20.0% and 37.0% (p=0.396); procedure-attributable events did not increase with age (11.1%, 6.7%, 3.7%; p=0.621), whereas disease-attributable events rose non-significantly (11.1%, 13.3%, 33.3%; p=0.138). Among 37 ruptured patients, Hunt & Hess grade III-V (OR 13.71, 95% CI 2.41-78.19) and vasospasm (OR 9.33, 1.68-51.88) were associated with major neurological complications. On adjustment, rupture status was associated (aOR 4.14, 1.02-16.85). Conclusions: Procedure-attributable complications with neurological deficit did not increase with age; the excess morbidity in older patients was either reversible or reflected hemorrhage severity. Chronological age alone should not preclude endovascular treatment; limited power renders these findings hypothesis-generating.

title: Spatial Distribution and Environmental Implications of Illegal Solid Waste Dumping along the Subangdaku River, Philippines
abstractText: Illegal dumping of solid waste along riverbanks is a major environmental concern that contributes to water pollution and the degradation of aquatic ecosystems, particularly in rapidly urbanizing communities. This study aimed to map and analyze illegal solid waste heaping points along the Subangdaku River in Sogod, Southern Leyte, Philippines. Specifically, the research identified the locations of illegal dumping sites, estimated the volume of accumulated waste, determined the composition of solid waste materials, and assessed selected water quality parameters of the river. Field surveys were conducted to locate dumping hotspots along the riverbanks, and the volume of waste heaps was estimated through measurements of heap area and average height. Waste composition was analyzed by categorizing collected samples into organic and inorganic components. Water samples were collected using grab sampling techniques and analyzed for temperature, pH, and dissolved oxygen following standard environmental monitoring procedures. Results identified four illegal solid waste heaping points along the river, with estimated waste volumes ranging from 0.35 m³ to 0.83 m³. Organic waste accounted for the largest proportion of the total waste composition, averaging 51.25%, while rubber materials comprised the lowest percentage. Water quality analysis indicated that the recorded temperature and pH values remained within the acceptable limits of national environmental standards. The occurrence of illegal dumping was largely associated with the proximity of residential settlements to the riverbanks and the uneven distribution of waste management facilities. These findings highlight the importance of strengthening solid waste management infrastructure, enhancing community awareness, and implementing effective riverbank protection strategies to reduce illegal dumping and protect river ecosystems.

title: Aristolochia dengii, a new species of subg. Siphisia (Aristolochiaceae) from China
abstractText: Aristolochia dengii, a new species of Aristolochia subg. Siphisia from Yunnan, China, near the border with Vietnam, is described and illustrated here. The species is remarkable for its flower with an extremely narrow opening and a saccate calyx limb. Morphologically, it is most similar to A. utriformis, but can be readily distinguished by its continuous, cylindric inner floral cavity from the upper tube through the throat to the calyx limb, whereas A. utriformis has a distinctly crateriform to conical throat that narrows toward the opening. The new species is currently known from only one population, comprising slightly more than 30 mature individuals. Given its extremely small population size and narrow distribution, it is provisionally assessed as Critically Endangered (CR).

Analisis Dampak Downtime Sistem Pembayaran Digital Terhadap Waktu Tunggu Pasien Menggunakan Pendekatan Interrupted Time Series Di Labkesda Kota Jambi.
abstractText: Digital transformation improves the efficiency of healthcare services but creates vulnerability to technical disruptions (downtime) and cyberattacks. This quasi-experimental study analyzes the impact of digital payment system downtime on pre-laboratory waiting time (from administrative registration to entry into the sampling room) at the Regional Health Laboratory (Labkesda) of Jambi City. Retrospective secondary data from electronic logs covered 67 effective working days (41 digital-phase days and 26 manual-phase days) and were analyzed using interrupted time series regression. Initial autocorrelation (Durbin-Watson = 0.917) was corrected using the Cochrane-Orcutt transformation (final n = 66; Durbin-Watson = 2.022; R² = 0.992). Mean waiting time increased from 1.99 minutes in the digital phase to 6.86 minutes in the manual phase. Downtime was accompanied by a level increase of 4.875 minutes (β₂ = 4.875; p < 0.001) and a negative trend change (β₃ = −0.021; p = 0.002), indicating a flattening trend that possibly reflects staff adaptation to manual procedures. Downstream patient-safety risks warrant anticipation but were not measured in this study. Management is advised to develop a business continuity plan comprising backup payment channels and manual contingency standard operating procedures (SOPs).
